samples.summary: JSDoc justifies omitting `onUndoJump` with a security assumption ("the read-only share view ... undo is disabled") that is false for editor-role share links
samples.evidence: The new prop doc says omitting `onUndoJump` "(the read-only share view) simply means no cross-tab undo, which is moot there since undo is disabled". But `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:198` computes `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, and line 300 mounts `<SheetView tabId={activeTabId} readOnly={readOnly} peerJumpTarget={peerJumpTarget} />` with no `onUndoJump`. A share-link visitor whose role is *not* viewer therefore has undo fully enabled while no cross-tab handler is registered: `Sheet.applyUndoSelection` hits `this.onUndoTabJump?.(selection)` with no listener (sheet.ts, otherTab branch) and the step is replayed into a tab the visitor is never switched to, i.e. a silent mutation of data outside the visible view. The mutation itself is within the editor role's rights, so this is an integrity/visibility gap rather than an authorization bypass — but the comment records a read-only property that does not hold, which is the kind of assumption a future reviewer will rely on when deciding whether a guard is needed.

samples.summary: New public `focusUndoSelection()` omits the `_readOnly` guard that every other public `Spreadsheet` method carries
samples.evidence: Every other public entry point on `Spreadsheet` opens with `if (!this.sheet || this._readOnly) return;` (lines 201, 222, 232, 243, 254, 304, 323, 333, 344, 364, 544, 554, 564, 598, 611, 624, 637, 650, 664, 726, 740, 781, 820, 830, 840, 850, 875-893). `focusUndoSelection` (line 689) checks only `!this.sheet || !selection.range`. Today it is non-exploitable — it calls `selectRow`/`selectColumn`/`selectStart`/`selectEnd` plus `render()`/`revealActiveCell()`/`notifySelectionChange()`, all of which a read-only mount already performs on click — so this is defence-in-depth only: the method is the odd one out in the class, and a future addition inside it (e.g. re-applying a style or committing an edit alongside the selection) would inherit no gate. `onUndoTabJump()` (line 678) likewise registers unconditionally, including from the read-only mount path in sheet-view.tsx.

samples.summary: Archived lessons doc records a step-by-step recipe for forging an authenticated session cookie
samples.evidence: The "Minting a dev session" section states that signing a JWT with the backend's `JWT_SECRET` and setting it as the `wafflebase_session` cookie yields a signed-in user, names `packages/backend/src/template/seed/register-templates.ts` as the reference implementation, and specifies the exact claim (`tokenType: 'access'`) that `JwtStrategy.validate` requires — confirmed against packages/backend/src/auth/jwt.strategy.ts:36. No secret value is disclosed and forging requires already holding `JWT_SECRET`, so this is not itself a vulnerability; it is an operational-hygiene note, since the doc lowers the effort for anyone who later obtains the secret (e.g. from a leaked dev env) and is committed to a public-facing repository tree.
